[i][b]The Birth of [nation]Al-Qadi[/nation]
[/b]
A secret meeting was held in a dark room, where the air was filled with the smell of incense and the expectation of a common goal. Supreme Leader Madhi Falah faced a makeshift table, and there was a map of the area laid out before him. Red circles and black arrows were marked on the map. Sitting next to him were delegates of sympathetic groups, undercover agents of the Special Delta Spears, and tribal authorities.

"My brothers," Falah began, his voice measured, "today, we act in response to the suffering of our people, due to foreign ideas and failed promises. The United Lavian Republic and its allies spread their evil throughout our land, insulting our faith. They impose their secular, misguided ways on the faithful, threatening not only our culture but the sanctity of Islam itself."

The room nodded silently in acquiescence. A desert camouflage-clad man held up his hand. "Supreme Leader, what of their strength? Their arms and intelligence? How are we to combat them?"
Falah smiled and nodded in the direction of a dark figure at the other side of the room. A man who was dressed in black, with an S.D.S. insignia on the sleeve of his jacket, came forward.
"Let me introduce this man from Special Delta Spears," Falah said. "He and his team will make sure we succeed."

The S.D.S. The agency declares, "We are of the Great Oceanic Republic. We observe that you require assistance against the Imperialist ULR. We will provide weapons, train you, and assist you in becoming a powerful force that the ULR cannot comprehend. The weapons that you will receive are AKs, BMPs, and even F-14s, which will be employed for justice. Together, we will establish a movement that transcends nations. The Al-Qadi will be the instrument of faith, fighting against corruption and foreign domination. We fought against your adversary, and the ULR will topple because the Party of the Oceanic Republic will soon end their imperialist goal!"

On the edge of the base, recruits from all over flocked, drawn by whispers of a sacred mission. Men and women of various occupations, like farmers, teachers, and soldiers, stood in line, some holding prayer beads, others anxiously holding AK-203s for the first time.

"Form up!" cried one of the instructors, a veteran S.D.S. operative. "You're not just soldiers, you're the chosen defenders of faith and justice. You'll learn to fight, to think, and to strike fear into the hearts of our enemies."

Over the next few weeks, the recruits underwent rigorous training. They learned to fire rifles, move through dense jungles, and lay ambushes. Discipline and dedication were emphasized, and their military training was woven in with sermons on their sacred mission.
[/i]
One of the recruits, a young man called Tariq, went to an old commander during a break. "Commander, will this lead to justice? Will we vanquish those who oppress us?"
The commander laid a hand on Tariq's shoulder. "Justice is not handed out, Tariq. It is seized. The Al-Qadi will demonstrate to all that faith cannot be silenced. With bravery and conviction, even the mighty ULR will falter."

At dawn on May 30th, the new commanders and troops convened in the middle of the camp. Al-Qad's emblem shone on the flags waving in the wind. Supreme Leader Falah ascended a raised platform.
"Today, we form a force that will go down in history. The Al-Qadi is more than a rebellion; it is a struggle for truth, faith, and the people that suffer. We will strike the enemy where they are most vulnerable and inspire those who have the most faith. Together, we will restore balance to a world full of greed and injustice."

The masses erupted into shouts of allegiance. Arms held up in unity, the trainees roared their oath in unison, "For faith, for freedom, for Al-Qadi!"
Al-Qadi's mission was conducted under the cloak of night, as a small group of operatives breached the facility, setting explosives on important machinery and leaving warnings of Al-Qadi's increasing presence.

By the time the sun rose, the complex lay in shambles, smoke providing evidence of how resolute the movement was. The attack was big news that spread like wildfire, drawing the attention of ULR authorities and recruiting new members to Al-Qadi's movement.

From the shadows of their secret hideout, Falah observed the world becoming aware. "This is just the beginning," he spoke softly. "The Al-Qadi will not rest until justice is achieved, and the oppressors are pushed out of our lands."
